questions.q: What driver does `docker network create northbridge-net` use by default?
options: host
none
bridge -- the same driver as Docker's default network
overlay, exclusively for multi-host clusters
questions.explain: A user-defined network created without specifying a driver uses the bridge driver, the same underlying driver as Docker's default bridge network.

questions.q: What is the real difference between the default bridge network and a user-defined bridge network like `northbridge-net`?
options: There is no difference -- they behave identically in every way
User-defined networks are faster at routing packets
Docker only runs its embedded DNS server on user-defined networks, so containers on them can resolve each other by name
The default bridge network does not allow any containers to communicate at all
questions.explain: Both use the same bridge driver and route traffic. The key difference is DNS: Docker's embedded name resolution is only active on networks you create yourself.

questions.q: How do `catalog` and `catalog-db` get attached to `northbridge-net`?
options: Automatically, the moment the network is created
With the `--network northbridge-net` flag passed to `docker run`, alongside flags like `-v` and `-p`
By editing the image's Dockerfile and rebuilding it
Only `docker network connect` can attach a container to any network
questions.explain: --network is just another docker run flag, used the same way -v and -p are -- all of them stack together on one command.

questions.q: On `northbridge-net`, what happens when `catalog-db` is removed and recreated with a new IP address?
options: catalog can no longer reach it under any circumstances
The name `catalog-db` keeps resolving correctly, because Docker's embedded DNS maps the name to wherever the current IP actually is
northbridge-net itself is automatically deleted and must be recreated
catalog-db permanently keeps its old IP address even after being recreated
questions.explain: This is the whole point of embedded DNS on user-defined networks: the name keeps resolving correctly even as the underlying IP changes across container restarts.

questions.q: What does `docker network connect` let you do that isn't possible with the default bridge network setup alone?
options: Attach a running container to an additional network without restarting it
Create a brand-new Docker image from a running container
Permanently merge two separate networks into a single one
Rename a container while it is running
questions.explain: docker network connect (and its counterpart, disconnect) can attach or detach a running container from a network on the fly, with no restart required.
